opener.label: Before any physics

steps.say: No equations yet, just judgement. Same size, so which block has more mass crammed into that space?
Now compare how much more is packed into the same space.

That 'mass packed into a space' is density: ρ = m ÷ V. Steel is 13 times denser than this wood. A ship floats by spreading its steel around a huge hollow volume, dropping its overall density below water's. Today: density ρ = m ÷ V, the wave equation v = fλ (both 'how much per unit'), and half-life (repeated halving).

opener.display:
A tiny steel nail sinks in water at once. Yet a steel supertanker, thousands of tonnes of the same steel, floats.
Two blocks help explain it. A wood block and a steel block are the same size (both 100 cm³). The wood weighs 60 g; the steel weighs 780 g.

steps: Waves: use v = fλ. Rearrange to f = v ÷ λ or λ = v ÷ f when needed.
Density: use ρ = m ÷ V. Convert cm³ to m³ (÷ 1 000 000) for kg/m³.
Half-life: find n = time ÷ half-life, then halve the activity n times (never divide by n).
State every answer with its unit: m/s, Hz, m, kg/m³ or Bq.
method_card.title: Waves, Half-Life and Density
method_card.content:
Three recall equations from different corners of physics. Waves: v = fλ, where speed is in m/s, frequency in Hz and wavelength in m. Density: ρ = m ÷ V, where mass is in kg and volume in m³ (1 cm³ = 0.000001 m³). Check whether your board gives you either equation.

Half-life needs no formula: each half-life the activity halves. Work out n = total time ÷ half-life, then halve the starting activity n times. To find a half-life from data, count how many halvings link the start and end activity, then divide the time by that count. Always finish with the correct unit.

steps: Multi-step waves: turn the period into frequency with f = 1 ÷ T, then use v = fλ.
Half-life from data: find how many halvings link the start and end activity, then half-life = time ÷ that number.
Always finish with a check and the correct unit.

steps: Pick the equation: v = fλ for waves, ρ = m ÷ V for density, or halve the activity for half-life.
Check the units are the base ones, then substitute the two known values straight in.
State the answer with its unit: m/s, kg/m³ or Bq.

steps: If a length is in mm or a volume in cm³, convert to metres or m³ before substituting.
If the unknown is not the subject, rearrange first: m = ρV, λ = v ÷ f, or f = v ÷ λ.
For a half-life from data, count how many times the activity halves, then divide the time by that count.

gold.hint: Count the halvings from 5400 to 675, then divide 60 by that count.
gold.display: A radioactive source has an activity of 5400 Bq. After 60 minutes its activity is 675 Bq. Calculate the half-life in minutes.

guided_steps.say: The activity drops from 5400 Bq to 675 Bq. Count the halvings, then divide the time by that count.

guided_steps.hint: How many times you divided by 2.

guided_steps.done: Gives the end activity 675 Bq, so a 20 minute half-life is right.

guided_steps.say: So the half-life is 20 minutes.

misconceptions.message: 5400 → 2700 → 1350 → 675 is 3 halvings, so half-life = 60 ÷ 3 = 20 minutes. Dividing 60 by the ratio 8 gives 7.5, which is wrong.

gold.hint: Find f = 1 ÷ T first, then λ = v ÷ f.
gold.display: An ocean wave has a speed of 15 m/s and a period of 8.0 s. Calculate (a) the frequency and (b) the wavelength.
gold.question: An ocean wave has a speed of 15 m/s and a period of 8.0 s. Calculate (a) the frequency and (b) the wavelength.

guided_steps.say: Two steps. Turn the period into frequency with f = 1 ÷ T, then find the wavelength with λ = v ÷ f.

guided_steps.pre: Check another way, λ = v × T = 15 × 8 =
guided_steps.done: Same 120 m, so the wavelength is right.

guided_steps.say: So (a) the frequency is 0.125 Hz and (b) the wavelength is 120 m.

misconceptions.message: First f = 1 ÷ T = 1 ÷ 8 = 0.125 Hz, then λ = v ÷ f = 15 ÷ 0.125 = 120 m. Using the period as the frequency (15 ÷ 8) gives about 1.9 m.

gold.hint: Density uses the total outer volume, including the hollow space: ρ = m ÷ V.
gold.display: A hollow steel ball has an outer volume of 120 cm³ and a mass of 250 g. Calculate the density of the steel ball in g/cm³ and explain why this is less than the density of solid steel (≈7.8 g/cm³).
options: 2.1 g/cm³: less than solid steel because part of the volume is air, not steel
7.8 g/cm³: the density is the same because the material is the same
2.1 g/cm³: less than solid steel because the ball is cooler
0.48 g/cm³: calculated using total volume without accounting for the shell

misconceptions.message: ρ = 250 ÷ 120 = 2.1 g/cm³. This is below solid steel (7.8) because the outer volume includes the hollow air space, not just steel.

gold.hint: Count how many halvings reach 50, then half-life = 96 ÷ that count.
gold.display: A gamma source decreases from 6400 counts/min to 50 counts/min in 96 minutes. Calculate the half-life. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

guided_steps.say: Count how many times you halve 6400 to reach 50, then divide 96 by that number.

guided_steps.pre: Keep halving to 50 (6400 → 3200 → 1600 → 800 → 400 → 200 → 100 → 50). Number of halvings, n =
guided_steps.hint: Count the steps from 6400 down to 50.
Divide 96 by 7 and round to 1 d.p.

guided_steps.done: Gives the end activity 50 Bq, so n = 7 and 13.7 min is right.

guided_steps.say: So the half-life is 13.7 minutes.

misconceptions.message: 6400 halves 7 times to reach 50 (6400 ÷ 128 = 50), so half-life = 96 ÷ 7 = 13.7 minutes. Using 6 halvings gives 96 ÷ 6 = 16 minutes.

gold.hint: f = v ÷ λ; divide the front numbers and subtract the powers of ten.
gold.display: An X-ray photon has a wavelength of 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ m and travels at 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. Calculate the frequency. Give your answer as a coefficient × 10¹⁸ (enter the coefficient, e.g. 3.0).
gold.question: An X-ray photon has a wavelength of 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ m and travels at 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s. Calculate the frequency. Give your answer as a coefficient × 10¹⁸ (enter the coefficient, e.g. 3.0).

guided_steps.say: Frequency f = v ÷ λ. Handle the powers of ten separately from the front numbers.

guided_steps.pre: The answer is 3.0 × 10¹⁸ Hz. Enter the coefficient =

guided_steps.say: So the frequency is 3.0 × 10¹⁸ Hz.

misconceptions.message: f = v ÷ λ = (3.0 × 10⁸) ÷ (1.0 × 10⁻¹⁰) = 3.0 × 10¹⁸ Hz, so the coefficient is 3.0. A power slip changes the exponent, not the coefficient.

gold.hint: Find how many half-lives fit in 12 hours, then the fraction left.
gold.display: A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 6 hours. A hospital needs it to have at least 25% of its original activity when it arrives. The transit time is 12 hours. Is the sample still usable on arrival?
options: Yes: 12 hours is 2 half-lives, leaving 25% of original activity
No: 12 hours is 3 half-lives, leaving only 12.5% of original activity
Yes: activity does not decrease significantly over 12 hours
No: any radioactive decay makes the sample unusable

misconceptions.message: n = 12 ÷ 6 = 2 half-lives, leaving (½)² = ¼ = 25%. Exactly 25% remains, just meeting the threshold, so the sample is usable.

bronze.hint: Multiply frequency by wavelength: v = fλ.
bronze.display: A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 6.8 m. Calculate the wave speed.
bronze.question: A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 6.8 m. Calculate the wave speed.

guided_steps.say: One equation: v = fλ. Both units are already right (Hz and m).

guided_steps.done: Gives back 50 Hz, so 340 m/s is right.
guided_steps.hint: Divide the speed back by the wavelength.

guided_steps.say: So the wave speed is 340 m/s.

misconceptions.message: v = f × λ, so 50 × 6.8 = 340 m/s. Adding the two (50 + 6.8) is not the wave equation.

bronze.hint: Rearrange to f = v ÷ λ, then divide.
bronze.display: A wave travels at 300 000 000 m/s with a wavelength of 0.10 m. Calculate the frequency.
bronze.question: A wave travels at 300 000 000 m/s with a wavelength of 0.10 m. Calculate the frequency.

guided_steps.say: Rearrange v = fλ to f = v ÷ λ. Units are already right.

guided_steps.done: Back to the speed, so 3 × 10⁹ Hz is right.

guided_steps.say: So the frequency is 3 × 10⁹ Hz (3 000 000 000 Hz).

misconceptions.message: f = v ÷ λ = (3 × 10⁸) ÷ 0.10 = 3 × 10⁹ Hz. Multiplying instead gives 3 × 10⁷ Hz, ten times too small.

bronze.hint: Divide mass by volume: ρ = m ÷ V.
bronze.display: An object has a mass of 500 g and a volume of 250 cm³. Calculate the density in g/cm³.

guided_steps.say: Units match (g and cm³), so density comes out in g/cm³. Use ρ = m ÷ V.

guided_steps.done: Back to the mass, so 2.0 g/cm³ is right.

guided_steps.say: So the density is 2.0 g/cm³.

bronze.equation_hint: \(\rho = m \div V\): units match (g and cm³), so answer is in g/cm³.

misconceptions.message: ρ = m ÷ V = 500 ÷ 250 = 2.0 g/cm³. Dividing volume by mass (250 ÷ 500 = 0.5) is upside down.

bronze.hint: One half-life means halve the count once.
bronze.display: A radioactive source has an initial count rate of 800 Bq. After one half-life, what is the count rate?

guided_steps.say: After each half-life the count rate halves. Here it is one half-life.

guided_steps.hint: The question says after one half-life.

guided_steps.done: Doubling returns 800, so 400 Bq is right.

guided_steps.say: So the count rate is 400 Bq.

bronze.equation_hint: After one half-life, the activity halves.

misconceptions.message: After one half-life the count halves: 800 ÷ 2 = 400 Bq. Leaving it at 800 forgets to halve.

bronze.hint: Find n = 15 ÷ 5, then halve that many times.
bronze.display: A source has an activity of 320 Bq. Its half-life is 5 years. What is the activity after 15 years?

guided_steps.say: Find how many half-lives fit in the time, then halve that many times.

guided_steps.done: Back to the start 320 Bq, so 40 Bq is right.

guided_steps.say: So the activity is 40 Bq.

bronze.equation_hint: How many half-lives in 15 years? Then halve that many times.

misconceptions.message: n = 15 ÷ 5 = 3 half-lives: 320 → 160 → 80 → 40 Bq. Stopping after two halvings leaves 80 Bq.

bronze.hint: Rearrange to λ = v ÷ f, then divide.
bronze.display: A radio wave has a frequency of 100 MHz (1×10⁸ Hz) and travels at 3×10⁸ m/s. Calculate its wavelength.
bronze.question: A radio wave has a frequency of 100 MHz (1×10⁸ Hz) and travels at 3×10⁸ m/s. Calculate its wavelength.

guided_steps.say: Rearrange v = fλ to λ = v ÷ f.

guided_steps.done: Back to the speed, so 3 m is right.

guided_steps.say: So the wavelength is 3 m.

misconceptions.message: λ = v ÷ f = (3 × 10⁸) ÷ (1 × 10⁸) = 3 m. Dividing f by v instead gives about 0.33 m, upside down.

bronze.hint: Divide mass by volume; the volume is already in m³.
bronze.display: A block of iron has mass 7.8 kg and volume 1.0 × 10⁻³ m³. Calculate the density in kg/m³.

guided_steps.say: Units are already kg and m³, so ρ = m ÷ V gives kg/m³.

guided_steps.done: Back to the mass, so 7800 kg/m³ is right.

guided_steps.say: So the density is 7800 kg/m³.

misconceptions.message: ρ = m ÷ V = 7.8 ÷ 0.001 = 7800 kg/m³. Multiplying (7.8 × 0.001 = 0.0078) is the wrong operation.

bronze.hint: Find n = 40 ÷ 10, then halve that many times.
bronze.display: A source has an initial count rate of 3200 Bq and a half-life of 10 minutes. What is the count rate after 40 minutes?

guided_steps.say: Find n, then halve n times.

guided_steps.done: Back to the start 3200 Bq, so 200 Bq is right.

guided_steps.say: So the activity is 200 Bq.

misconceptions.message: n = 40 ÷ 10 = 4 half-lives: 3200 → 1600 → 800 → 400 → 200 Bq. Stopping at three halvings leaves 400 Bq.

silver.hint: Count the halvings from 1000 to 125, then divide 30 by that count.
silver.display: The activity of a radioactive isotope falls from 1000 Bq to 125 Bq in 30 days. Calculate the half-life.

guided_steps.say: You are given the start and end activity. Count how many halvings link them, then divide the time by that count.

guided_steps.hint: How many times you divided by 2.
Divide the time by the number of halvings.

guided_steps.done: Gives the end activity 125 Bq, so a 10 day half-life is right.

guided_steps.say: So the half-life is 10 days.

silver.equation_hint: How many times do you have to halve 1000 to reach 125? Then divide total time by that number.

misconceptions.message: 1000 → 500 → 250 → 125 is 3 halvings, so half-life = 30 ÷ 3 = 10 days. Dividing 30 by the activity ratio 8 gives 3.75, which is wrong.

silver.hint: Convert 0.15 mm to metres first, then f = v ÷ λ.
silver.display: An ultrasound pulse travels at 1500 m/s in soft tissue. The pulse has a wavelength of 0.15 mm. Calculate the frequency in Hz. (1 mm = 0.001 m)
silver.question: An ultrasound pulse travels at 1500 m/s in soft tissue. The pulse has a wavelength of 0.15 mm. Calculate the frequency in Hz. (1 mm = 0.001 m)

guided_steps.say: The wavelength is in millimetres but the speed is in metres per second. Convert λ to metres first.

guided_steps.hint: Divide speed by the wavelength in metres.

guided_steps.done: Back to the speed, so 10 000 000 Hz is right.

guided_steps.say: So the frequency is 10 000 000 Hz (10 MHz).

silver.equation_hint: Convert wavelength to metres first, then \(f = v \div \lambda\)

misconceptions.message: Convert first: 0.15 mm = 0.00015 m, so f = 1500 ÷ 0.00015 = 10 000 000 Hz. Forgetting to convert gives 1500 ÷ 0.15 = 10 000 Hz, a thousand times too small.

silver.hint: Rearrange to m = ρ × V, then multiply.
silver.display: A wooden block of density 0.80 g/cm³ has a volume of 500 cm³. Calculate its mass in grams.

guided_steps.say: You want mass, so rearrange ρ = m ÷ V to m = ρ × V. Units g/cm³ and cm³ give grams.

guided_steps.done: Gives back 0.80 g/cm³, so 400 g is right.
guided_steps.hint: Divide the mass back by the volume.

guided_steps.say: So the mass is 400 g.

misconceptions.message: m = ρ × V = 0.80 × 500 = 400 g. Dividing instead (500 ÷ 0.80 = 625) is the wrong way round.

silver.hint: 25% is 2 half-lives; multiply 2 by the half-life.
silver.display: A sample of carbon-14 has a half-life of approximately 5700 years. A fossil bone has 25% of the original carbon-14 activity. Estimate the age of the fossil.

guided_steps.say: 25% is a quarter. Count how many halvings take you from 100% to 25%, then multiply by the half-life.

guided_steps.pre: Number of half-lives to reach 25%, n =

guided_steps.hint: Multiply the number of half-lives by 5700.

guided_steps.say: So the fossil is about 11 400 years old.

misconceptions.message: 25% is a quarter: 100% → 50% → 25% is 2 half-lives, so age = 2 × 5700 = 11 400 years. Using one half-life gives 5700 years.

silver.hint: Convert 600 cm³ to m³ (÷ 1 000 000), then ρ = m ÷ V.
silver.display: A stone has a mass of 1.62 kg. When placed in a measuring cylinder it displaces 600 cm³ of water. Calculate the density of the stone in kg/m³.

guided_steps.say: Density in kg/m³ needs the volume in m³. Convert cm³ to m³ first: divide by 1 000 000.

guided_steps.hint: Divide mass by the volume in m³.

guided_steps.done: Back to the mass 1.62 kg, so 2700 kg/m³ is right.

guided_steps.say: So the density is 2700 kg/m³.

silver.equation_hint: Convert cm³ to m³ (÷ 1 000 000), then \(\rho = m \div V\)

misconceptions.message: Convert 600 cm³ to 0.0006 m³ first, so ρ = 1.62 ÷ 0.0006 = 2700 kg/m³. Skipping the conversion gives 1.62 ÷ 600 = 0.0027, far too small.

silver.hint: Rearrange to λ = v ÷ f; dividing by 0.5 makes it bigger.
silver.display: A seismic P-wave travels at 6000 m/s through rock. If it has a frequency of 0.5 Hz, calculate its wavelength.
silver.question: A seismic P-wave travels at 6000 m/s through rock. If it has a frequency of 0.5 Hz, calculate its wavelength.

guided_steps.say: Rearrange v = fλ to λ = v ÷ f. Watch out: dividing by 0.5 makes the answer bigger.

guided_steps.hint: Dividing by 0.5 is the same as multiplying by 2.

guided_steps.done: Back to the speed, so 12 000 m is right.

guided_steps.say: So the wavelength is 12 000 m (12 km).

misconceptions.message: λ = v ÷ f = 6000 ÷ 0.5 = 12 000 m. Multiplying instead (6000 × 0.5 = 3000) is wrong; dividing by 0.5 must make it bigger.

problem_bank.gold_description: Multi-step problems: chain two wave steps, read decay data, or reason about density and usability.
problem_bank.bronze_description: One equation with the values already in the right units: v = fλ, ρ = m ÷ V, or a whole number of half-lives.
problem_bank.silver_description: Convert a unit or rearrange the equation first, or find a half-life by counting halvings in the data.
